subject: EverHome latency surge — stabilization snapshot & customer commitments
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] EverHome latency surge — convene bridge

Team,

We just got alerts for elevated tail latency affecting EverHome's production model endpoint in us-west-2. Customer impact: increased request timeouts and degraded streaming responses. I spun up an emergency bridge — dialing in now (see Zoom link below). Primary asks for this first touch:

- Ben/Infra: confirm if any autoscale/driver failures or node preemptions in the us-west-2 GPU pool.
- Aditya/Runtime: capture kernel failures, OOM, or KV-cache regression; attach quick grep of runtime logs to the thread.
- Laura/CS: prepare a short executive note for the customer (2-3 bullets + commitments).
- Evelyn/Support: validate if this affects other accounts in the same shard.

Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210 (hosted by me)
Incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/EH-2026-10-27

I'll draft the initial external update once we confirm the scope. Please join the bridge if you can — even 15 minutes of focused triage helps.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge-log-snippets.txt (excerpted logs)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] EverHome latency surge — convene bridge

On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 8:15 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
>
> We just got alerts for elevated tail latency affecting EverHome's production model endpoint in us-west-2.

Quick update from runtime: we are seeing a sharp increase in tokenization/serving latency tied to a rolling change in the kernel selection logic deployed as part of 2026.10.24. The heuristic that selects cuBLAS vs. custom attention kernels is misclassifying some mid-length sequences, forcing an expensive fallback path.

Actions taken (08:20–08:40 PDT):
- Flipped kernel-selection flag to the conservative path (roll back) — immediate 35% improvement in median; tail still elevated.
- Identified three nodes with degraded NVLINK performance — we isolated and cordoned them for drain.
- Collected runtime traces and attached a trimmed log sample (bridge-log-snippets.txt).

Proposed external message (for Laura to send):
- Acknowledge issue and scope (some EverHome traffic in us-west-2 experienced increased latency and intermittent timeouts).
- What we did (rolled back kernel-selection, cordoned nodes) and measurable improvement.
- Short commitments: (1) full postmortem within 72 hours with root cause and mitigation, (2) expanded alerting/thresholds for kernel-selection regressions, (3) follow-up call tomorrow morning with engineering leads.

I'll continue tracing tail paths; ping me in bridge for deeper trace slices.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Helen Young <helen.young@everhome.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@everhome.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: EverHome — stabilization snapshot and immediate commitments

Helen —

Thank you for your patience this morning. I wanted to share a brief, plain-language update from Redwood on the latency surge affecting some EverHome traffic in us-west-2. Our engineering team is on the bridge and has implemented targeted mitigations. Key points: 

- What happened: a runtime kernel-selection regression caused a subset of mid-length requests to fall back to a slower execution path, increasing tail latency and causing intermittent timeouts for some streaming sessions.
- What we did: we rolled back the kernel-selection change and cordoned three affected GPU worker nodes. Those mitigations produced an initial improvement in request times.
- Impact: At peak ~0.8% of EverHome requests experienced timeouts; the majority of traffic has returned to normal but we are monitoring tail latency closely.

Immediate commitments:
1) We will provide a detailed postmortem to EverHome within 72 hours (root cause, timeline, corrective actions).
2) Daily progress reports until we close the incident (next update EOD Wed).
3) A follow-up technical call tomorrow at 09:00 PT with our runtime lead (Aditya) and your ops team to walk the timeline and mitigations.

Attachments: EverHome-exec-commitments.pdf (one-page summary), incident-timeline.csv (trimmed timeline)

Please let me know if you want the follow-up call moved or if there are additional stakeholders we should loop in. We take this seriously and will own the follow-through.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Helen Young <helen.young@everhome.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@everhome.com>, ops@everhome.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EverHome — stabilization snapshot and immediate commitments

Laura,

Thanks — appreciate the fast response and the clear commitments. A few quick asks from our side: 

- Can Redwood provide access to the trimmed runtime traces (or a sanitized artifact) for our SRE team to review before tomorrow's call?
- We would also like the daily progress update to include the rolling 99.9th percentile graph for the last 48 hours.
- SOC logs request: our compliance team will need the audit logs for the affected window (Oct 27 07:30–10:30 PT) to validate session continuity for our internal auditors.

We're good with the 09:00 PT technical call tomorrow. Helen will be joined by Carlos and our platform SRE.

—Helen
Helen Young
VP, Platform Engineering
EverHome
